title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Analysis situs, 4th draft, July 1986). The ambient is a 1‑dimensional 'tame' (piecewise‑linear / cellular) space with a set M of cells: M_0 = L are the vertices (points) and M_1 are the open edges, with incidence a ⊲ X meaning 'a is an endpoint of X'.
- A préfigure Φ is a set of cells.
- supp°(Φ) is the union of the open cells in Φ; supp(Φ) is the union of their closures.
- A figure is a closed préfigure (it contains the endpoints of its edges). Φ̄ is the closure of Φ.
- A préfigure is normalised, or 'irredondante' (monadique, lisible): it has no vertex of order 2 lying in Φ. Such a vertex would let two adjacent open edges and the point between them merge into one larger open edge.

The previous page proved the main theorem. Every constructible subset S is supp° of a unique irredundant préfigure P. P_1 consists of the maximal 1‑dimensional cells of S. P_0 = (∂P_1 ∩ S) ⊔ {isolated points}.

Item 2) on this page treats closure. For a constructible S there is a smallest closed constructible set containing it, namely S̄. If S = supp°Φ, then S̄ = supp°(Φ̄) = supp(Φ̄).

The warning is that normalisation is not preserved by closure. Take Φ = two adjacent open edges with the common vertex omitted. This Φ is irredundant, but Φ̄ contains that vertex with order 2 and so is redundant. (The written sentence and the margin sketch with an interior point seem to state this the other way round; the mathematics forces the direction just given.)

Item 3) announces a combinatorial description of constructible sets via normalised préfigures.

On 4 July the aim becomes an 'autodual' presentation, meaning symmetric under passage to the complement. To get it one must separate two kinds of points:
- the isolated points of Φ (vertices in Φ of order 0);
- the points of L that are not in Φ but are adherent to it, i.e. Φ̄∖Φ.

He sets Φ_1 = Φ̄ ∖ {isolated points}, a figure that need not be irredundant. It is irredundant iff Φ̄∖Φ ⊂ ∂Φ = {s : ord(s,Φ) = 1}, i.e. iff Φ has no 'interior frontier points' (missing vertices with order 2).

The implicit duality: an interior frontier point of Φ is exactly an isolated point of the complement. So the complement S ↦ X∖S exchanges isolated points with interior frontier points, and boundary points with boundary points.

The next page develops the 'zoologie des sommets' by order 0/1/2: isolated, boundary (proper/improper), interior.
errors: The sentence 'Φ̄ peut fort bien être normalisé, si Φ ne l'est pas', as transcribed, has the direction reversed. The correct phenomenon, and the one consistent with the criterion at the bottom of the page, is that Φ can be normalised while Φ̄ is not (an interior frontier point becomes an order‑2 vertex of the closure). This is either a slip of the pen or a misreading.
The displayed equality 'S = Supp°(Φ̄) = supp(Φ̄)' should read S̄ (the closure of S) on the left. Otherwise it would only hold for closed S.
'ordre de s dans Φ̄ est 1' is presumably meant as order relative to Φ (whose edges are the same as those of Φ̄), so the statement is harmless.

ideas.what: Unique irredundant (normalised) cellular representation of constructible subsets of a 1‑dimensional tame space; closure computed on the representation, with normalisation not preserved by closure.
ideas.modern_name: Canonical (coarsest) cell decomposition adapted to a definable set in dimension 1; o‑minimal / semialgebraic cell decomposition; stratifications of graphs
ideas.usually_credited_to: o‑minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s); semialgebraic cell decomposition: Łojasiewicz, Hironaka, Shiota
ideas.where_published: Only the programme of 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the 1986 Analysis situs notes are unpublished

ideas.what: 'Autodual' description of constructible sets, symmetric under complement. Isolated points of S correspond to 'interior frontier points' (points of the closure, not in S, of order 2), i.e. isolated points of the complement.
ideas.modern_name: Complement duality for constructible/definable sets of a 1‑dimensional stratified space; vertex classification by local degree

ideas.what: Criterion: Φ̄ minus its isolated points is irredundant iff Φ̄∖Φ ⊂ ∂Φ (no interior frontier points).
ideas.modern_name: Elementary combinatorial lemma on vertex orders in a graph

deep.surprise_reason: This is elementary combinatorics of constructible subsets of a 1‑dimensional cellular space: closure, normalisation, and the classification of isolated, boundary and interior frontier points. It is a working page of Grothendieck's unpublished tame‑topology project and historically interesting as such. But the content is standard in o‑minimal or semialgebraic cell decomposition and contains no result a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'un plus petit support constructible formé' is likely 'fermé'. The intended statement is the smallest closed constructible set containing S, i.e. S̄.
Displayed formula: the left‑hand side should probably be read S̄ (overlined), not S.
'Celle l'est ssi' should be 'Elle l'est ssi'.
'points de L qui ne sont pas dans Φ, mais adhérents : Φ dans M' likely reads '...adhérents : Φ̄ ∖ Φ' (dans L).

Margin top: 'Aussi facile ! Facile : c'est aussi supp°(S̄) ?'. The margin labels 'Φ normalisé / Φ̄ non normalisé' should be checked against the sketch, since mathematically Φ (vertex missing) is normalised and Φ̄ (vertex present between two edges) is not.
